target.title: fix: keep mapped hook content provenance scoped [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using multiple hook mappings could have a non-Gmail hook treated as Gmail-sourced when the request body included a matching `source` value. That could make external hook content skip the wrapping behavior the operator expected for the actual mapping.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mapped hook provenance now comes from the matched hook path and resolved hook session key instead of a caller-controlled body field. The Gmail path and Gmail-scoped sessions still keep Gmail provenance; unrelated mappings stay classified as webhook content unless their own mapping explicitly opts into unsafe external content.

Maintainer note: Gmail-scoped behavior is now tied to `/hooks/gmail` or `hook:gmail:` session provenance, not body-source-only custom mappings. Custom mappings that only send `source: "gmail"` in the body will be treated as webhook-scoped after this change.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

## User Impact

Operators can keep Gmail-specific unsafe external content settings enabled without that setting spilling over to unrelated hook mappings. Existing Gmail hooks and explicit mapping-level unsafe-content configuration continue to work as before.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox focused validation on head `74b5c41b3b8b2a442251efca71a3f68496f4d8dd`: `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts`
- Result: `run_9f9f3fc54731`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_09d75e0f940a`, 50 hook tests passed across the gateway projects.
- Added regression coverage for `/hooks/github` receiving `source: "gmail"` while dispatching with `externalContentSource: "webhook"` and no unsafe-content override.
- AWS Crabbox live Gateway hook POST proof on the same head: `run_1c7045ee011c`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_09d75e0f940a`, command `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --id cbx_09d75e0f940a --timing-json --script /tmp/openclaw-hook-proof.OD2kCS.sh`.
- Denied/fixed live POST: `POST /hooks/github` with body `source=gmail` returned `200` and dispatched `sourcePath=/hooks/github`, `sessionKey=hook:webhook:github`, `externalContentSource=webhook`, `allowUnsafeExternalContent=null`; no policy call/request/access to Gmail-scoped unsafe-content inheritance occurred.
- Positive live control: `POST /hooks/gmail` returned `200` and dispatched `sourcePath=/hooks/gmail`, `sessionKey=hook:gmail:proof`, `externalContentSource=gmail`; Gmail route/session provenance still works.
- Live proof gap: no external model/provider call was made; the external agent runner boundary was replaced with a recorder so the hook dispatch payload could be shown directly.
